Rationale: Collection, project, shopping/display, magazine/library and camera contexts support the stable show/display verb sense.
Talent-show, watch-a-show, presenter and theatre/actor contexts support the stable programme/performance noun sense.

These flat, phrase-adjacent, or weak narrative contexts do not reliably distinguish display, performance, guide/show-around, exhibition, or another use. Hold rather than broaden existing identities; the three partitions cover all 22 current occurrences exactly once.
Sensory and food/eating contexts support the action of tasting or sampling; preserve the stable taste#sample identity.
Fresh/different and sour/sweet food-adjective contexts support the linking-predicate flavour sense; preserve taste#flavour.
Mooncake type, lotus-seed and bean vocabulary provides positive evidence for taste as a food-flavour noun rather than the tasting action or linking predicate.
Food, spicy/salty/sour/bitter, delicious and yucky contexts support the ordinary food-taste adjective; unrelated dictionary senses are not learner evidence.
Class/grade and middle-school/life contexts support the school-term noun; terminology, legal-term and algebra senses are not current textbook evidence.
Bad-life, unpleasant-food and mistake/failure contexts support strong negative evaluation. The adverbial dictionary extension is not separately evidenced.
